description: ETSI TTCN-3 Conformance Suite execution baseline. Generated by `ntt conformance` against testdata/ttcn3-conformance-tests/. A file 'matches' when the interpreter's actual outcome (verdict, parse-error, semantic-error) equals the file's @verdict annotation, with a relaxation: `error`/`fail` verdicts also satisfy `@verdict pass reject` annotations because an interpreter-first implementation catches semantic violations at runtime rather than compile time. Files annotated as 'inconclusive' are counted as 'skipped' and excluded from the pass-rate denominator.

Internal canaries were inventoried and recorded as a coverage baseline. PRIOR: 95.15% -> 95.17% (+1 matched, timer read virtual clock). Titan-parity phase 5, the read timer operation (ETSI 23.4): `T.read` now reports elapsed time against a per-testcase virtual clock that `T.timeout` fast-forwards to the timed-out timer's deadline, instead of a tick-counter fraction (Ticks/MaxTicks) of the timer's declared duration. A freshly started timer still reads exactly 0.0 because no timeout has advanced the clock (Sem_2304_001/002 preserved); `running` keeps the tick-counter cap so spin loops on `t.running` still terminate and `t.read` inside them stays a monotonic 0.0 (Sem_2302_001 preserved); and a `t_timer.read` taken after a sibling `t_aux.timeout` now sees t_aux's 1.0s duration rather than a 20.0-duration timer's 0.25*20=5.0 tick fraction, so the reading lands in the expected [1.0, 1.05] window deterministically (no wall-clock jitter). TimerHandle.StartedAtVirtual records the virtual start at `.start`; TestcaseExec.virtualClock is advanced monotonically (never backward) by every `.timeout` (both the bare-selector and call forms). Gain: Sem_2304_timer_read_003. PRIOR: 95.07% -> 95.15% (+4 matched, value attribute introspection via declared type). A new env side-binding records each definition's declared type name (recordDeclaredType in evalValueDecl/evalTemplateDecl incl. the type-directed struct branch); the value-path selector consults it via the type's TypeDesc, falling back to the value's scope when the type carries no such attribute. The `variant` kind is excluded - a codec-associated variant (`variant "Codec"."Rule"`) is not retrieved by the unqualified `.variant` form and needs the separate variant(encoding) machinery (so Sem_2708_003/004 are preserved). When the type's own encode equals the inherited one the variant context is unchanged and the inherited variant still applies. A type synonym (`type R S`) now records its referenced type (TypeDesc.Underlying) so field access and inheritance follow the underlying record while the synonym's own `with` attrs form an enclosing layer above it. Each type's directly-declared attributes are tracked separately (TypeDesc.OwnAttrs/OwnLocal) so the chain consults a type's OWN non-@local attribute, never an inherited or @local-confined one. Gains: Sem_27010200_general_008 (synonym field inherits the underlying record's encode, not the synonym's own), 009 (synonym field with no underlying encode inherits the synonym's encode). Titan-parity phase 5, type/field attribute introspection (ETSI 27.1.2 / 27.7): `R.field.encode` / `.variant` now resolves by following the field's declared type. Precedence: (1) a field-qualified override on R (`with { encode(field) "X" }`); (2) the encode/variant R carries with the `override` keyword, which propagates onto contained fields and supersedes the field's own type attribute; (3) the field's declared type's own attribute (field-type-following); (4) the enclosing-scope default. The `override` modifier is now captured per kind (TypeDesc.Override, computed in typeDescForScoped/collectWithAttrs from WithStmt.Override) and is told apart from `@local` - both populate WithStmt.Override, but `@local` confines the attribute to the definition and does NOT propagate, so only the literal `override` keyword sets the propagation flag (restored 010/011 which use `encode @local`). Gains: Sem_060203_records_and_sets_of_single_types_026/030/034/038 (record-of and set-of, integer-array and named record-of indexers). PRIOR: 94.42% -> 94.46% (+2 matched, index-range arrays). Element storage and value equality are unaffected (an offset array still compares equal to a 0-based value literal of the same elements, `v == {200,3,4,5}`). Plain `v[N]` / record-of / set-of keep 0-based indexing. Gains: Sem_060207_arrays_020/021. PRIOR: 94.37% -> 94.42% (+2 matched net: +5 omit-matching, -3 codec accidental-pass). Titan-parity phase 5, distinct `omit` value (ETSI 6.2/15.9/Annex B): the TTCN-3 `omit` special value is now a dedicated runtime sentinel (runtime.Omit) separate from Undefined (uninitialised/unmodelled). The decisive semantic fix is matching: `match(presentValue, omit)` now correctly returns FALSE - omit matches only another absent value (omit or the Undefined wildcard), `*` (AnyValueOrNone) still matches omit, and `?` (AnyValue, which requires a present value) no longer matches omit. Everywhere omit must behave like an absent field, Omit mirrors Undefined: equality (singelton.Equal treats OMIT/UNDEFINED as the same absent value, so `v == { omit, ... }` and `x == omit` work), the presence predicates (ispresent/isbound/isvalue all report omit as absent), sizeof skips omit fields, indexing an omit value yields Undefined, and the implicit field-expansion path (ETSI 6.2.1.1) materialises a record when a subfield of an omitted field/record is assigned - including deep chains through several omitted intermediates (v_rec.sub := omit; v_rec.sub.field1.subfield1.nested1 := 0) via storeReceiver. We do not model codec default-value decoding, so those three previously passed ONLY because the omitted field was conflated with the `?`/Undefined wildcard and over-matched the concrete default - a semantically incorrect match that the omit fix correctly removes.
